meta.subject: Semaglutide (GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide analog) - FTO/exclusivity pipeline worked example
meta.note: Patent numbers and expiry dates below were pulled directly from the FDA Orange Book patent_info pages for each NDA and cross-checked against Google Patents (mirrors USPTO grant data). EPO/litigation entries are as reported by the secondary sources cited - re-verify against the EPO Register and PACER/USPTO PTAB records before relying on them for a real decision. This file is illustrative, not a legal FTO opinion.

molecule.class: Acylated GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide analog

regulatory_classification.reason: 31 residues, below the FDA's 40-amino-acid drug/biologic dividing line (Section 505 FDCA vs Section 351 PHS Act)
regulatory_classification.nce_exclusivity_status: 5-year NCE exclusivity from first approval (Ozempic, Dec 2017) already expired; patents, not regulatory exclusivity, are the current binding constraint on generic entry

products.indication: chronic weight management / obesity, cardiovascular risk reduction, MASH

structural_modifications_vs_native_glp1.rationale: Steric block at the DPP-4 cleavage site; confers resistance to dipeptidyl peptidase-4 mediated inactivation.
structural_modifications_vs_native_glp1.conserved_in_claims: Composition-of-matter claims typically recite position 7/8 substitution with a non-proteogenic amino acid as a genus, not just Aib specifically - check the exact Markush variable before assuming Aib is the only substituent claimed.

structural_modifications_vs_native_glp1.semaglutide_residue: Lys (retained; side-chain epsilon-amine carries the lipidation conjugate)
structural_modifications_vs_native_glp1.rationale: Sole attachment point for the AEEA-AEEA-gammaGlu-C18-diacid albumin-binding tail once position 34's lysine is removed.
structural_modifications_vs_native_glp1.conserved_in_claims: The conjugate's chain length, linker chemistry and attachment chemistry are claimed as a genus (variable acyl chain length/linker) in the compound patents - this is the single highest-value claim element to map precisely against any design-around.

structural_modifications_vs_native_glp1.rationale: Removes the second acylation-competent lysine so that conjugation occurs exclusively at position 26, giving a single, defined conjugation product instead of a mixture.
structural_modifications_vs_native_glp1.conserved_in_claims: Often claimed together with the position-26 conjugation as part of the same genus.

conserved_structural_motifs.name: Position-8 Aib substitution (DPP-4 resistance)
conserved_structural_motifs.figure_color: used in the residue-swap panel (red highlight)
conserved_structural_motifs.why_conserved: This is close to a structural necessity for oral/systemic peptide stability against DPP-4; almost every long-acting GLP-1 analog in this class (liraglutide, semaglutide, and most follow-ons) makes some change at this position.
conserved_structural_motifs.claim_relevance: Look for Markush language covering 'a non-natural amino acid at position 8' rather than 'Aib' specifically - the genus is usually broader than the one exemplified residue.

conserved_structural_motifs.name: Position-34 Lys-to-Arg substitution
conserved_structural_motifs.figure_color: used in the residue-swap panel (red highlight)
conserved_structural_motifs.why_conserved: Needed whenever the design conjugates only at Lys26 and wants to avoid a mixture of mono- and di-acylated product.
conserved_structural_motifs.claim_relevance: Frequently claimed jointly with the Lys26 conjugation limitation rather than as its own independent claim.

conserved_structural_motifs.name: Lys26 side-chain conjugate: AEEA-AEEA-gammaGlu-C18 diacid
conserved_structural_motifs.type: acylated albumin-binding side chain (the actual Markush genus in the compound patents)
conserved_structural_motifs.note_on_smiles: The peptide backbone is modeled as an N-acetyl/N-methylamide-capped lysine for clarity (a standalone, drawable fragment) rather than the full 31-residue peptide; stereochemistry at the Lys and Glu alpha-carbons is omitted from the SMILES for legibility (both are L-configured in the native molecule).
conserved_structural_motifs.why_conserved: This is the actual pharmacophore for half-life extension - it is what US8129343's claim 1 genus covers ('acylated at Lys26 with a moiety containing at least two acidic groups, one terminal, attached via a hydrophilic linker'). Every once-weekly GLP-1 in this structural class carries some version of it.
conserved_structural_motifs.claim_relevance: Highest-priority element for a chemist's design-around review: check the claimed range on (a) acyl/diacid chain length (patent text cites 4-40 carbons), (b) linker composition (hydrophilic spacer, not necessarily AEEA specifically), and (c) number of acidic groups on the distal end, before assuming a modified chain length or linker falls outside the genus.

orange_book_patents.title: Use of long-acting GLP-1 peptides
orange_book_patents.litigation: Challenged by Viatris via IPR (petition granted 2023; oral argument July 2024; PTAB decision expected Oct 2024 - outcome must be re-verified)

ozempic_nda_209637.litigation_status: Settled with Mylan/Natco, Dr. Reddy's, Apotex and Sun Pharma in fall 2024; generic entry reported around 2032.

orange_book_patents.claim_type: method of use (MASH/NASH with liver fibrosis)

wegovy_nda_215256.litigation_status: Active infringement litigation against Mylan, Sun Pharmaceuticals and Apotex reported as of early 2025 - re-verify current status.
wegovy_nda_215256.note: The Federal Circuit's Teva v. Amneal decision has been cited as calling into question whether device/method patents that do not require semaglutide itself should be Orange-Book-listed at all - a possible delisting risk that would shorten this list.

regulatory_exclusivity.description: method of treating type 2 diabetes mellitus

rybelsus_nda_213051.formulation_note: SNAC (salcaprozate sodium) absorption enhancer is central to the oral tablet's later-filed formulation patents (2033-2034 expiries) - this cluster, not the compound patent, is now the long pole for Rybelsus generics.

epo_and_international.status: Upheld by EPO Opposition Division against inventive-step challenges (2024-2025); appeal possible.
epo_and_international.note: Reported alongside multiple OTHER Novo Nordisk semaglutide-related EPO patents that the Boards of Appeal have revoked in the same period - the EU compound/formulation estate is more contested than the US one and needs its own jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction check, not an assumption that US outcomes carry over.

fto_risk_summary.reasoning: Nearest-term expiries (2026 and 2031); the 2023 Mylan IPR challenge to the extended-term compound patent failed, but the earliest-filed compound patent is already at or near expiry.

Latest expiries (2033-2041), squarely the subject of Novo Nordisk v. Mylan claim-scope litigation, and not cleared just because the compound patents expire - a 'skinny label' design-around is a regulatory/legal lever here, not a chemistry one.

fto_risk_summary.risk_tier: high (single point of failure for Rybelsus)
fto_risk_summary.item: Oral formulation / SNAC-related patents (9278123 and later Rybelsus-specific filings, 2031-2034)
fto_risk_summary.reasoning: Rybelsus is the one format where a single formulation claim cluster can hold off generic entry well past the compound patent's expiry - the absorption-enhancer chemistry needs its own design-around track.

fto_risk_summary.item: EPO oral-formulation and other semaglutide-related EU filings
fto_risk_summary.reasoning: Mixed outcomes at the EPO (some upheld, some revoked on appeal) mean the EU picture cannot be assumed to mirror the US Orange Book position.

fto_risk_summary.item: Regulatory exclusivity (NCE / competitive generic therapy / indication-specific exclusivities)
fto_risk_summary.reasoning: 5-year NCE exclusivity already lapsed; remaining exclusivity codes are indication-specific and narrower than the patent estate, so patents - not exclusivity - are the actual gating constraint today.
